content.text: I fixed the parser, but nothing is committed yet. **What broke:** In today's run, Step 3 failed when it tried to read the OpenCode Zen pricing page. That page now shows a sale price as `Mistral Large 4 (50% off)$1.36 $0.68…`. The parser read the crossed-out old price and the new price together as one value, `"$1.36 $0.68"`, and refused it. So the run kept yesterday's Zen pricing file and exited with code 1. Because of that, the mapping and data commits, the site build and the deploy were all skipped. Copilot, OpenCode Go and ClinePass pricing, the benchmark data and the scoring all finished fine. **Fix** in [src/opencode-zen/parser.ts](src/opencode-zen/parser.ts): - The parser now ignores crossed-out text (`` and `` tags) along with footnote markers, so a sale cell reads as the current price. - It removes a `(N% off)` suffix from the model name, so the model keeps the name `Mistral Large 4`. The discount is saved in `notes` as "Promotional pricing (50% off)." instead. I tested it on today's live page: all 103 rows parse, and Mistral Large 4 comes out at $0.68 input, $2.09 output and $0.07 cached read. Typecheck, lint and format all pass. I didn't run the full `npm start`, because it rewrites the files under `data/` and could start the local parser-repair agent. **Not causing the failure, but worth knowing:** - 47 models are skipped for "incomplete benchmark data", including the GPT 5 and 6 models and every Claude model. Only 75 candidates got scored. Benchmark data comes from Artificial Analysis on the free tier (`tier: free`), which may now leave some fields out. That's worth checking if the rankings look thin. - OpenCode Go has some "no matching row in: requests" warnings for the variants split by context length (GPT 6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5). The pipeline isn't dropping any data. Artificial Analysis (the benchmark source) simply hasn't published coding and agentic scores for these models yet, and our scorer skips any model that's missing a score.

**What I found** (34 benchmark entries behind the 47 skip messages, since several providers share entries):
- **25 of 34 have an intelligence score but no coding or agentic score.** That includes all the Claude and GPT 5.x/6 models, Grok 4.7, GLM 5, MiniMax M2.5 and MiMo v2.6.
- **5 are missing only agentic** (GPT 5, 5.1, 5.4, Qwen3.6 Plus, Kimi K2.5), **2 are missing only speed** (DeepSeek V4 Flash, LongCat 2.0), and **2 have nothing at all** (GPT 5.4 Pro, GPT 5.5 Pro).
- **This isn't new.** Every snapshot since September 17 has the same gaps, and no model has lost a score.
- **The free tier probably isn't the cause.** The feed includes coding and agentic scores for Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT 6 Astra, which are just as new and high-end. I can't fully confirm without a paid key, but the gaps look like models Artificial Analysis hasn't tested yet.
- **The gaps depend on the model's age:**
  - Older models were released before those scores existed. Only 12 of 186 models from before mid-2025 have them.
  - Brand-new models haven't been tested yet: Opus 5.5 (released Sep 22), Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28), GPT 6.1 Sol (Sep 29), Haiku 5.5 (Oct 7).
  - Opus 5.5 is ranked first overall on intelligence, but we can't score it.

**Why the skip happens:** [compute-scores.ts:198-210](src/scoring/compute-scores.ts:198) requires every score to be present. All four categories give the agentic score some weight (from 5% in `codeReview` to 50% in `agenticCoding`), so a model without it is skipped everywhere.

**What I'd recommend:** keep the rule, but stop hiding the skipped models.
- Filling in made-up scores or spreading the weight over the other scores would rank frontier models on partial data. That would quietly favour or penalise exactly the models people care most about.
- Instead, I can add an "awaiting benchmarks" list to `recommendations.json` and the site. It would name the models we skipped and which score each is missing. The models then join the rankings on their own once Artificial Analysis publishes their scores, with no further work needed.

The other option is to score with whatever data a model has and spread the missing weight over the rest. Rankings would then include the new models right away, but each ranking would rest on different data, and I'd mark those entries as partial.

There's also a separate set of 14 "no Artificial Analysis mapping" skips (Gemini 3.x, GPT 5.4, Qwen3.8 Flash and others). Those may just need entries in `config/model-mapping.json`.

Should I build the "awaiting benchmarks" list, or would you rather have the partial scoring?

I'll make a missing score count as zero toward the model's total. Ranges will still be computed only from models that have that score. The alternative, setting the raw value to 0, would drag every range's minimum down to 0 and distort everyone else's normalized scores. Each scored model will also list which scores it was missing.

I made the change: models that are missing some benchmark scores are now ranked, with each missing score counted as zero. I haven't committed it yet. When I ran scoring on today's data, the number of ranked models went from 75 to 118, but the recommendations stayed almost the same.

**What changed in [compute-scores.ts](src/scoring/compute-scores.ts):**
- A missing score adds nothing to the model's total. That puts it level with the lowest-scoring model that does have the score.
- The scale for each score is set only by the models that have it. If I stored missing scores as a real 0, the bottom of every scale would drop to 0 and everyone else's numbers would shift.
- Each scored model now lists the scores it's missing (`missingMetrics`). The breakdown shows those as null, which the site already displays as "–".
- Models with no benchmark data at all are still skipped, since they would be ranked on price alone. That's only GPT 5.4 Pro and GPT 5.5 Pro.
- The log now says "Partial benchmark data … scored as 0" for each of these models instead of "Skipping".

**What it does to the rankings:**
- None of the newly ranked models makes a top-2 list. The only changes are in `llmWiki`. On OpenCode Go, Qwen3.8 Max replaces DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp. On Zen, the same two models swap places, which comes from the price scale widening with more models, not from a new entry.
- Zeroing the agentic and coding scores pushes the newest frontier models near the bottom. On Copilot (27 models):

| Category | Claude Opus 5.5 | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | GPT-6.1 Sol |
|---|---|---|---|
| agenticCoding | 19th | 18th | 21st |
| codeReview | 16th | 17th | 19th |
| softwareFactory | 20th | 18th | 23rd |
| llmWiki | 15th | 14th | 17th |

Your coding-focused categories weight the agentic and coding scores at 50–70%, so a model missing both has almost no chance to rank well. In practice "zero when missing" means "listed, but ranked last until Artificial Analysis publishes its scores". That's fair if you want only proven models recommended. If you were hoping to see Opus 5.5 near the top now, this won't do it.
